title: Turn it and turn it (Avot 5:22)
hook: Ben Bag Bag: turn it and turn it, for everything is in it
tomorrow: opening night's done. was the work worth it either way?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bold as a leopard, with a face that can still blush. Today, the boldest thing a reader can do: go back.

A comfort show, watched for the fifth time, and suddenly a joke you never caught. A song on repeat that lands differently the week everything changes. Same words, new thing. So why read the same old text again and again? Ben Bag Bag, a sage in Avot with a name like a drumbeat, answers with a verb you can do with your hands.
screen: `THE FIFTH REWATCH.` → `SAME WORDS, NEW THING.` → `WHY READ IT AGAIN?`

segments.voice: Ben Bag Bag says of the Torah: turn it and turn it, for everything is in it. Look into it. Grow gray and old over it. Don't move from it, for you have no better portion than it. Turn it: the way you turn a stone in your hand to see the side that was facing down. The text stays the same. The light changes, and so do you. A line read young and read again with gray hair is the same ink and a different reading. You've already watched this happen on this path. A few days ago, the ten sayings. Someone turned Genesis one, counted the and God saids, and found only nine. The Talmud turned it again and found the tenth hiding in the first words: in the beginning. Nobody added a word. Someone just turned it one more time. Notice the end of the saying, too. Grow gray over it. Ben Bag Bag doesn't picture a finish line. He pictures a reader who keeps coming back, until the hair changes color and the text still hasn't run out. Everything is in it is less a claim you can check in an afternoon than an invitation to try: turn it, turn it, and see.
screen: `TURN IT, AND TURN IT AGAIN.` · `SAME TEXT, NEW LIGHT.` · `THE TENTH SAYING, FOUND BY TURNING.` · `GROW GRAY OVER IT.` · then, large: `TURN IT, TURN IT.`

segments.voice: Take one short line you know by heart: a verse, a saying from this path, even a lyric. Say it out loud slowly, three times, leaning on a different word each time, and listen to how the meaning tilts. For the rest of the sit, keep turning it silently.
screen: `ONE SHORT LINE.` · `THREE TIMES, A NEW WORD LEANED ON.` · `KEEP TURNING IT.`

segments.voice: Turn it and turn it: Ben Bag Bag's advice for the Torah. The same text, read again, from a new side.
screen: `TURN IT AND TURN IT — today's word`.

segments.voice: One to hold: turn it, turn it, because everything is in it and nothing runs out. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Jewish study the same texts are read again every year: the Torah is read through in a yearly cycle in the synagogue, and learners return to the same pages of Mishnah and Talmud, often with a study partner.
